past_medical_history: Sudden onset of slurred speech and right facial weakness 5 months ago, resolved within 48 hours; MRI at the time showed an acute lacunar infarct

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person, place and year, month incorrect. MoCA 21/30 with losses in trail-making, clock, digit span backwards, serial sevens, fluency (9 animals) and delayed recall (3/5 unaided, 5/5 cued). Marked abulia: he answers in single words, initiates nothing, and shows long latencies. His wife says he is 'switched off'.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Visual fields full. Right nasolabial fold slightly flat, residual from the stroke. Speech mildly dysarthric, fluent, with reduced output.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk, tone slightly increased on the right. Strength 5/5 throughout with slightly reduced right-sided speed.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 3+ on the right, 2+ on the left, right plantar equivocal.
neurological_exam.coordination: Slowed right finger tapping, no dysmetria.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal base and stride with slightly reduced right arm swing. Tandem gait possible. No falls.
neurological_exam.additional: Marked reduction in spontaneous speech and gesture with preserved comprehension. No frontal release signs. Pulse regular at 74.

patient.chief_complaint: Since a small stroke five months ago he has become passive, slow and unable to organise anything
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Marco Ruggeri is a 72-year-old retired postal supervisor who attends with his wife five months after a lacunar stroke. The stroke itself was mild: slurred speech and a droop of the right face that resolved within two days, with an MRI at the time showing an acute lacunar infarct. What has not resolved is a change in behaviour that his wife describes as him being 'switched off'. He rises only when told to, sits without occupation for hours, has stopped his allotment and his card games, and answers questions in single words after a long pause. He is not sad and denies depression; he simply does not begin anything. Cognitively his wife reports that he cannot organise: he no longer manages the accounts, cannot plan a shopping trip, and gets confused when two things happen at once. His memory improves when he is given the context. The change dates entirely to the stroke; before it he ran the household administration and the allotment without difficulty. There have been no further events, no falls, no hallucinations, no fluctuation and no dream enactment.

additional_observations: The genu lesion interrupts the anterior thalamic peduncle and the inferior thalamic radiation, disconnecting the dorsolateral prefrontal and anterior cingulate circuits — the anatomy of capsular genu syndrome
The infarct corresponds to the acute lacunar lesion imaged five months ago and is now chronic
The additional small-vessel burden is Fazekas 2 with one further lacune, insufficient by itself to explain a dementia

mri.impression: Chronic strategic infarct at the left genu of the internal capsule extending into the caudate head, on a background of moderate small-vessel disease. The lesion disconnects prefrontal-subcortical circuits and accounts for the abulia and dysexecutive syndrome; the Fazekas 2 burden is a contributor but not sufficient alone.

labs.interpretation: HbA1c 7.6% shows imperfect glycaemic control. LDL 84 mg/dL on high-intensity statin remains above the post-stroke target of 70 mg/dL. TSH, B12, folate, RPR and HIV are normal or negative, excluding reversible causes.

quantitative_data.pattern: dysexecutive with initiation failure, recognition and language spared

specialized_test.impression: A severe dysexecutive syndrome: fluency and set-shifting at the 2nd-3rd percentile with only one Wisconsin category completed, against normal naming, comprehension and recognition memory. The dissociation between impaired initiation and intact instrumental language is characteristic of frontal-subcortical disconnection rather than of cortical degeneration.

clinical_assessment.impression: MoCA 21/30 with severe abulia and executive failure, cue-responsive recall, and language spared apart from reduced output. The syndrome is one of impaired initiation with intact instrumental language, which localises to the frontal-subcortical circuits interrupted at the genu of the internal capsule and the caudate.

results.title: Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement
results.authors: Sachdev P, Kalaria R, O'Brien J, et al.
results.summary: Requires a cognitive syndrome documented on a validated instrument plus imaging or temporal evidence that cerebrovascular disease accounts for it.

results.title: Neuroimaging standards for research into small vessel disease (STRIVE-2)
results.authors: Duering M, Biessels GJ, Brodtmann A, et al.
results.summary: Defines and standardises the reporting of white matter hyperintensity, lacunes, microbleeds, perivascular spaces and cortical superficial siderosis.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

medication_review.proposed: review of the current medication list for anticholinergic burden
warnings: Anticholinergic load is a reversible contributor to cognitive impairment in this population and should be quantified before any new prescription.
medication_review.summary: No prohibitive interaction identified within the current list.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Vascular dementia — strategic single-infarct type, capsular genu syndrome from a left internal capsule genu and caudate infarct, on a background of moderate small-vessel disease

differential.key_features: Abulia after a basal ganglia stroke is regularly diagnosed as depression, but he denies low mood, the Geriatric Depression Scale is 3/15 and the Apathy Evaluation Scale is 56 — this is abulia from circuit disconnection, and it responds to different management

The Fazekas 2 burden contributes but does not reach the threshold at which small-vessel disease alone explains a dementia; the abrupt onset dated to the genu infarct identifies the strategic mechanism
Abrupt onset dated to a stroke, no progression in five months, cue-responsive recall and normal hippocampi
Apathy is prominent but there is no disinhibition, no loss of empathy, no compulsivity, no frontotemporal atrophy and no gradual onset
No fluctuation, hallucinations, parkinsonism or dream enactment

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a collateral history from an informant who sees the patient daily: the shape of the decline (abrupt, stepwise or gradual), whether any step can be dated to a cerebrovascular event, and which instrumental activities have been lost
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Abrupt change dated precisely to a lacunar stroke five months earlier, with abulia and executive failure disproportionate to a resolved mild motor deficit, and no progression since

optimal_actions.action: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MoCA 21/30 with severe abulia (Apathy Evaluation Scale 56), executive failure and cue-responsive recall, disproportionate to a resolved mild motor stroke

optimal_actions.action: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, HbA1c, lipid panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reversible causes excluded; HbA1c 7.6% and LDL 84 mg/dL identify the two vascular targets still short of goal after a stroke

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms — FLAIR for white matter hyperintensity with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI to establish that the lesions are chronic, and SWI for microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis — together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Chronic strategic infarct at the left genu of the internal capsule extending into the caudate head, 0.9 mL, on a Fazekas 2 background with preserved hippocampi

optimal_actions.action: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Dysexecutive syndrome with severe initiation failure and preserved recognition memory and language — a frontal-subcortical disconnection profile

optimal_actions.action: Confirm the diagnostic criteria applied and the current secondary-prevention targets against the guidelines
optimal_actions.expected_finding: VASCOG 2014 criteria and the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary prevention targets confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Institute full secondary prevention after a lacunar stroke: blood pressure toward a systolic below 130 mmHg, HbA1c below 7.5%, LDL below 70 mg/dL, single antiplatelet therapy continued, and structured activity scheduling with occupational therapy for the abulia rather than an antidepressant trial by default
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Secondary-prevention targets set for a lacunar mechanism and the abulia managed behaviourally as a disconnection syndrome rather than as depression

optimal_actions.action: Disclose the diagnosis and its mechanism to the patient and the informant, and address driving, medication management, finances, advance care planning and caregiver support
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Patient and informant engaged in care planning; safety domains addressed

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change

critical_actions: Date the cognitive change against the stroke — onset within three months satisfies the temporal criterion
Distinguish abulia from depression with formal scales before starting an antidepressant
Document the executive and initiation deficit with formal testing, since the screen understates it
Obtain brain MRI and localise the infarct: the genu of the internal capsule is a strategic site
Institute secondary prevention for a lacunar mechanism, including glycaemic control
Provide activity scheduling and caregiver education for the abulia, which the patient cannot initiate himself
contraindicated_actions: Do not treat abulia as depression by default; an antidepressant is not the first answer to a disconnection syndrome
Do not dismiss a cognitive syndrome as disproportionate to a mild stroke — strategic lesions are defined by that disproportion
Do not anticoagulate: the mechanism is small-vessel occlusion and there is no embolic source
Do not prescribe anticholinergic bladder agents for his prostatic symptoms
key_reasoning_points: The genu of the internal capsule carries the anterior thalamic peduncle and the inferior thalamic radiation; a lesion there disconnects prefrontal and cingulate circuits and produces abulia with a dysexecutive syndrome out of proportion to its size
A mild motor stroke that resolves can leave a severe cognitive syndrome; the disproportion is the diagnostic clue, not a reason to doubt the attribution
Abulia and depression are dissociable on formal scales and the distinction changes management from antidepressant to activity scheduling
Impaired initiation with intact naming and comprehension is a subcortical disconnection pattern, not a cortical degenerative one
The coexisting Fazekas 2 burden matters for prognosis and for risk-factor control even though it is not sufficient to explain the dementia by itself

red_herrings.data_point: A mild stroke that fully resolved
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests the stroke was too small to account for a dementia, prompting a search for a coincident degenerative disease
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Strategic infarcts are defined by producing deficits disproportionate to lesion volume; a 0.9 mL lesion at the capsular genu disconnects prefrontal circuits bilaterally

red_herrings.data_point: Apathy after a basal ganglia stroke
red_herrings.intended_effect: Diagnosed as post-stroke depression and treated with an antidepressant
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: He denies low mood with a Geriatric Depression Scale of 3/15 and an Apathy Evaluation Scale of 56; this is abulia from circuit disconnection and it calls for activity scheduling rather than an antidepressant trial

key_educational_points: Capsular genu infarction produces abulia and a dysexecutive syndrome by disconnecting thalamocortical projections
Deficits disproportionate to lesion volume are the signature of the strategic-infarct mechanism
Abulia is not depression, and the formal scales separate them
A resolved motor stroke can leave a permanent cognitive syndrome
